# NOTES: "The Case of the Black Twenty-Two" by Brian Flynn (1929, Grosset & Dunlap; Gutenberg #75209)

## Structure
25 chapters (I–XXV), one book. Chapter titles run I "Mr. Daventry Receives a Commission" through XXV "The Riddle of the Black Twenty-Two".

## Cast
- **Peter Daventry**: junior partner, "Merryweather, Linnell and Daventry, Solicitors", Cornhill, London. Oxford man, drinks, witty, impulsive. Brother of **Gerald Daventry** (accountant, Wedderburn and Rathbone, Devonshire Place; M.C.C. member).
- **David Linnell**: senior partner, 58, Lancashire-born, shrewd, prim about waste of words.
- **Plunkett**: middle-aged clerk, 35 years' service.
- **Merryweather**: founder, dead seven years.
- **Collins**: office messenger sent for catalogue.
- **Laurence P. Stewart**: American millionaire (Chicago, Wall Street), widower, age 53 (birthday 22 July), collector obsessed with Mary, Queen of Scots; claims descent from her. Bought Assynton Lodge (near Wantage, Berkshire Downs). Murdered.
- **Charles Stewart**: son, ~22, tennis player; hides engagement to **Rosemary Armitage** of "The Towers" (7 miles away).
- **Marjorie Lennox**: father's ward since age 3; petite, blue eyes, retroussé nose, handkerchief with "M. L." initials. Accuses Llewellyn. Flushed cheeks.
- **Morgan Llewellyn**: secretary, early 30s, pince-nez, reddish-brown eyes, Welsh. Writes love letter to Marjorie threatening her guardian.
- **John Butterworth**: butler, 60+, ex-Sir Julian Kennedy's butler (Washington). Wife is housekeeper (married 37 years). Murderer of Laurence Stewart. Daughter **Alice Mortimer** (née Butterworth). Legacy £500 p.a.
- **Colonel Leach-Fletcher**: neighbour, "Neuve Chapelle" bungalow, Rockinge road; Bentley car; dined at Assynton 7–10 pm; mentioned book Renan's *Vie de Jésus*.
- **Sergeant Amos Clegg**: local Assynton police, Romantic, married 17 years.
- **Constable Potter**: guards library.
- **Detective-Inspector Goodall**: Scotland Yard, stout, clean-shaven, double-breasted blue serge suit; wife; "Pelmanism" jibe.
- **Anthony Bathurst**: amateur investigator, grey eyes, Uppingham, Oxford contemporary of Gerald; excels at ball games; solved Considine Manor affair; lives in flat (maid Emily).
- **Ronald Forshaw** (young), **Mr. Day** (tall, partner, Day, Forshaw and Palmers).
- **Edward Druce**: night-watchman, ~60, wizened, daughter Poppy; reports woman who sneezed.
- **James (Jim) Mason**: night-watchman, murdered at Hanover Galleries.
- **Mrs. Turner**: cleaner.
- **Doctor Archer** (Galleries); **Doctor Gunner** (Assynton).
- **Patrick O'Connor**: boot-boy, 18 (b. 17 March), bicycle.
- **Michael O'Connor**: foundry giant, black beard, black eyes, 6 ft 2.
- **Maidment**: gardener.
- **Barton, Regan, Evans, Winter**: maids; **Mrs. Briggs**: cook.
- **Andrew Ferguson**: of Crake and Ferguson, NY, Stewart's solicitors; arrives on *Mauretania*.
- **"Snoop" Mortimer / "Flash Alf"**: NY crook, alias "Laurence Charles Stewart"; wife **Alice** (hay fever, dark glasses; alias "Mrs. Stewart"). Waring: Goodall's assistant.
- **Blanchard**: hotel proprietor, Blanchard's Hotel, Clifford Street W.; fair eyelashes, bird-like; clerk; porter **Atkins**; chambermaid **Rabjohns**; receptionist Miss Fortescue.
- **Gustave**: waiter at the Violette (Oxford St). **Lironi**: proprietor.
- **Marriott**: Peter's friend at Violette.
- **Forshaw Junior** and **Mr. Day** at the Galleries.

## Places
Cornhill office; Hanover Galleries (Day, Forshaw and Palmers, W.1); the Violette restaurant; Leyton cricket ground (Middlesex v Essex); Princes Club (squash); Paddington station; Assynton Lodge (Berkshire); Assynton village; Red Dolphin inn; Neuve Chapelle; Ricardo's (Soho); Clifford Street hotel; British Museum.

## Objects
- Lot 37: Collar of Pearls. Lot 38: Antique Tapestry Fire-screen (Mary's Royal Lion top-left, fleur-de-lis top-right, Leopards and Lilies bottom corners; beads spell "JESUS CHRIST, GOD AND SAVIOUR"). Lot 39: Rosary of Amber Beads.
- Hanover Galleries screen and Assynton (Museum Room) screen: metal-work screen; Latin "Timeo Danaos" (Virgil, Aeneid II "Timeo Danaos et dona ferentes") incised center; Fish in center (Greek ICHTHUS acrostic = Jesus Christ God Saviour); hidden cavity behind fish's eye/tail.
- The "Black Twenty-Two": 22 black pearls of Lorraine, gift of Cardinal of Lorraine to Mary; hidden in metal screen's fish cavity; wrapped in discoloured cotton wool.
- Museum Room catalogue: 2,044 items; crown of Charles I; gorget of Black Prince; musk-ball of Henry VIII.
- Catalogue no. 866: "Antique fire-screen, of beaten metal-work… originally property of Mary, Queen of Scots."
- Memoirs of Réné de St. Maure, "One-time Page to Mary Stuart" (book with bullet in it, 848 pages, bookcase): passage about Thibaut Girardier, Chief Armorer, two screens, "the Black Twenty-Two".
- Revolver: Stewart's, 5 chambers loaded, 1 fired, found in LEFT pocket of dressing-gown.
- Murder weapon: jagged stone (~14 in, bottle-neck) from rockery path, thrown into pool; retrieved by Peter barefoot.
- Ink-bowl with mud pellets and four brown stones (from coal-scuttle).
- Telegrams: "Say! What the hell's biting you—when I say Buy—then Buy. Got that? Stewart." and "Say—you don't look before you leap—you take a magnifying glass. Same name as before."
- Note on desk: "Urgent in the morning! M. L."
- Personal ad (Daily Telegraph, Mon 30 May): "M. S. Ring Regent 9999 till further notice. Both well!" ("Both well" = Bothwell).
- Blanchard's telephone: Regent 9999.
- Tennis: Charles at The Towers.

## Timeline
- **Day 1 (Thu 9 June?)**: Peter at Cornhill; Linnell reads Stewart letter (dated June 7th) ordering purchase of Lots 37–39 at sale Friday June 10th, 1pm. Peter lunches at Violette; overhears couple; blurts "So's Mary, Queen of Scots"; man sweeps cruet; woman says "let's go to-morrow". Peter views items at Galleries; plain-clothes men watch. Linnell telegrams Stewart; reply. Peter dines at Club, Isthmian/"On Approval".
- **Night (8/9 June)**: Mason murdered at Galleries (~11 pm–midnight); woman "decoy" asks about Galleries opening times and Marble Arch direction; items stolen. Assynton: Stewart killed ~11pm (struck 3 times) after Colonel leaves 10pm; Charles heard voice ~9:45; Butterworth heard two voices at 10:10 incl. Marjorie.
- **Day 2 (Fri 10 June, dated murder discovery)**: Linnell at Galleries; Goodall; Druce's statement. Phone call from Charles to Cornhill. Peter and Linnell; Peter to Leyton, then meets Bathurst at Princes.
- **Evening**: Peter, Bathurst, Goodall board 6:55 from Paddington; met Clegg at Assynton; stay at Assynton Lodge.
- **Night 1**: Bathurst hears step at 1:22 am, sees Llewellyn enter room next but one.
- **Day 3 (Sat)**: Bathurst walks, meets Michael O'Connor at foundry; tar on bicycle tyres; bicycle in Maidment's potting-shed. Library reconstruction; coal-scuttle stones; Museum Room; "geometry": circle radius 1 mile centre Hanover Galleries → Blanchard's Hotel, Clifford St (trunk call 11 min). Stewarts from New York.
- **Afternoon**: Museum Room — screen missing. Marjorie reveals 'Timeo Danaos' and fish. Clegg reports Blanchard's.
- Bathurst visits Colonel: book Renan on desk; Colonel's disclosures (underhand work; Charles's conduct).
- Peter discovers Llewellyn's letter in *Vie de Jésus*; stone retrieved from pool; bullet found in Memoirs; Peter fires two shots (no sound heard upstairs).
- Bathurst goes to London: Blanchard's Hotel (Atkins, Rabjohns; hay-fever clue; "Asthma Cure"); supper at Ricardo's with Goodall.
- **Next**: Bathurst at British Museum; Times/Telegraph; Telegraph ad; Mon 30 May phone number.
- **Monday**: Ferguson arrives; will: £250,000 to Marjorie, residue to Charles; conditional on marriage to each other; Llewellyn £300 p.a.; Butterworth £500 p.a. Inquest adjourned.
- Bathurst orders house closed; Butterworth remains.
- Night: Mortimers and Alice caught in library by Goodall; Mortimer arrested for Mason murder; Butterworth for Stewart murder.
- Final: Bathurst opens fish cavity; 22 pearls; Charles: "glad Girardier picked the right screen"; Bathurst: "So am I."

## Key Clues / Deductions
- Locked door and bolted doors = faked by Butterworth (only three had keys/knowledge).
- "M. L." = Merryweather, Linnell and Daventry (Bathurst's solution).
- Bullet in Memoirs; stone in pool; ink-bowl debris; tar on bicycle; light switch; Renan book with letter.
- Butterworth had Morgan's letter removed? (Llewellyn's letter in book).
